newsitem.title: JAPAN: Not yet time to change band on baht - Bank/Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Not yet time to change band on baht - Bank/Thailand.

text.p: The time is not to right to change the exchange rate mechanism of the baht, although the currency is slightly weak against the dollar, Jaroong Nookhwan, the deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand said on Saturday.
Asked whether the bank had any plans to widen the band set on the baht's fluctuations, he told Reuters : "No, it is not the time," but added that a baht at 26 to the dollar was a "bit weak."

On Friday, the Thai unit came under intense pressure against the U.S. dollar on rumours, denied by the central bank, that the baht band would be widened. Traders in Singapore said the bank had intervened in that market to prop up the baht by selling dollars at 26.025 baht.

Nookhwan, who is in this southern Japanese city to attend the 30th annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank, also shrugged off concerns that Thai banks were over-exposed to loans made to the property sector, which is seen to be in financial trouble.
The percentage of property loans made by Thai banks was not as high as widely perceived to be, Nookhwan said.
"(The percentage is at around 10 percent for the big banks. It's not too high. For the banking system, it's ok," he said.
Asked whether the bank may cut rates in the future to prop up the economy, Nookhwan only said that interest rates depend on market mechanism and did not elaborate.
